title: Consultancy Services for the Design, Development, and Deployment of an Online (web-based) Dashboard for the Climate FIRST Project in Papua New Guinea
description: Global Green Growth Institute in Papua New Guinea seeks to engage a competent consulting firm to support the Design, Development, and Deployment of an Online (web-based) Dashboard for the Climate FIRST Project in Papua New Guinea.PROJECT OBJECTIVES AND BACKGROUND:Papua New Guinea (PNG) is among the countries most vulnerable to the impacts of climate change, facing increasing risks to its people, ecosystems, and economy. In response to these challenges, PNG has made significant commitments under the Paris Agreement, including the submission of its Enhanced Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC) and development of its National Adaptation Plan (NAP), outlining ambitious targets to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and enhance climate resilience across sectors.To support these national climate priorities, the Global Green Growth Institute (GGGI), with funding from the Australian Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade (DFAT), is implementing the Climate Finance Initiative for Resilience and a Sustainable Transition (Climate FIRST). Developed by GGGI, Climate FIRST is a catalytic bilateral initiative under the PNG–Australia Climate Change Action Plan (PACCAP). The program is designed to assist PNG in accessing and coordinating climate finance and strengthening institutional systems to deliver a high-quality pipeline of climate change adaptation and mitigation investments aligned with national plans and priorities. GGGI serves as the delivery partner for the initiative and implements it in close collaboration with the Climate Change and Development Authority (CCDA).Climate FIRST forms part of the broader strategic partnership between the Government of Papua New Guinea and the Government of Australia to enhance climate resilience, support inclusive low-emission development, and improve climate finance governance. The program aligns closely with PNG’s Medium-Term Development Plan, Climate Compatible Development Strategy, and the NDCs. DFAT’s support reflects Australia’s commitment to fostering effective, transparent, and coordinated climate action across the Pacific.A key component of Climate FIRST is the establishment and operationalization of the Climate Finance Steering Committee (CFSC), mandated under Section 15G of the Climate Change (Management) Act 2015. The CFSC is designed to function as a high-level national coordination platform, responsible for screening, reviewing, and endorsing climate finance project ideas and proposals in line with PNG’s strategic climate and development goals. The Committee is supported by the Climate Finance Unit (CFU) within CCDA and is advised by GGGI through targeted technical assistance.To support the CFSC’s operationalization and enable more effective pipeline management, GGGI seeks to develop a secure, web-based Climate Finance Dashboard. This platform will serve the institutional needs of the CFSC, CFU, GGGI, and DFAT by strengthening coordination, transparency, and information management throughout the climate finance project cycle in PNG.Objectives of this AssignmentThe objective of this assignment is to design, develop, and deploy a secure, web-based Climate Finance Dashboard to support the Climate FIRST initiative. The dashboard will serve as a centralized platform for climate finance coordination, project pipeline management, and institutional collaboration between the Climate Finance Steering Committee (CFSC), the Climate Finance Unit (CFU) within the Climate Change and Development Authority (CCDA), the Global Green Growth Institute (GGGI), and the Australian Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade (DFAT).Specifically, the dashboard is expected to:1) Enable structured submission and workflow management of climate finance project proposals through a digital platform aligned with the CFSC’s screening and endorsement process. The system should allow project proponents to submit ideas, and track proposals through stages such as technical review, CFSC clearance, and pipeline inclusion—while maintaining secure records of decisions, inputs, and timelines.2) Function as a centralized data repository for climate finance projects under Climate FIRST, capturing information across the full project lifecycle—from early-stage concepts to approved, funded, and implementing investments. The system should support version control, audit trails, and archiving proposal documents.3) Provide advanced data visualization and real-time analytics capabilities to support evidence-based decision-making. Users should be able to filter and analyze projects by sector, investment size, funding source, project type, geographical coverage (national and subnational), implementation stage, and alignment with PNG’s national strategies, including the NDC, NAP, Medium-Term Development Plan, and the Climate Compatible Development Strategy.4) Integrate a dynamic, map-based interface to visualize project activities across PNG’s provinces and districts. The map should allow users to apply thematic filters (e.g., donor, sector, or implementing partner) and drill down to subnational levels to identify gaps, overlaps, and investment opportunities.5) Enhance institutional coordination and stakeholder engagement by incorporating tools for managing partner profiles, tracking roles and responsibilities, documenting engagement activities, and storing meeting records. This will enable transparent collaboration among CCDA, DFAT, GGGI, and other national and development actors.6) Monitor the financial status of pipeline projects, including secured, pledged, and under-negotiation funding, and co-financing contributions. A finance-tracking module should allow DFAT, CCDA, and GGGI to view funder types, financial flows, and leverage ratios to support transparency and reporting.7) Support monitoring, evaluation, and learning (MEL) by linking project records to performance indicators, aggregating data across outputs and outcomes, and enabling the generation of automated progress reports for internal review, donor reporting, and government briefings.8) Implement robust role-based access control to ensure differentiated permissions and secure collaboration across multiple user types—such as administrators, reviewers, proposal submitters, and observers—based on institutional roles within the Climate FIRST governance structure.9) Adhere to international standards of usability, data protection, and system resilience, including the integration of multilingual user interfaces, offline back-up protocols, and secure hosting infrastructure to ensure accessibility, continuity, and compliance with best practices in digital public infrastructure.The dashboard is envisioned as a critical enabler of Climate FIRST’s institutional strengthening objectives—supporting real-time collaboration, transparency, and the effective mobilization of climate finance in Papua New Guinea.PROPOSED ACTIVITIES & DETAILED SCOPE OF WORK:GGGI is seeking a qualified consulting firm or service provider to design, develop, and deploy a secure, web-based Climate Finance Dashboard to support climate finance coordination, project pipeline management, and stakeholder collaboration under the Climate FIRST initiative. The system must be robust, user-friendly, and adaptable to the evolving needs of climate finance governance in PNG. It should enhance coordination between the Climate Finance Steering Committee (CFSC), the Climate Finance Unit (CFU) within the Climate Change and Development Authority (CCDA), GGGI, and the Australian Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade (DFAT).The scope of work includes the full life-cycle development of the Climate Finance Dashboard—from inception and system design to deployment, training, and post-launch support over a 12-month period. The Consultant will work closely with GGGI, CCDA, DFAT, and members of the Climate Finance Steering Committee to ensure the platform is co-designed, user-friendly, secure, and fully aligned with PNG’s institutional workflows and climate finance governance framework.The assignment will be delivered through the following key activities:1) Inception and Co-Design Phase1.1 Conduct inception meetings with GGGI, CCDA, DFAT, and key CFSC stakeholders to confirm expectations and clarify roles.1.2 Carry out a comprehensive needs assessment, including technical and functional user requirements gathering across national and subnational levels.1.3 Review relevant policy documents, existing MEL frameworks, climate finance workflows, and reporting tools.1.4 Submit an inception report including a detailed work plan, system blueprint, wireframes, and proposed methodology for dashboard design and development.2) System Architecture and Design2.1 Develop a modular and scalable system architecture that supports core dashboard components: project submission and tracking, finance monitoring, MEL integration, and stakeholder engagement.2.2 Design user interfaces that are mobile-responsive, intuitive, and aligned with the roles and responsibilities of key users (e.g., administrators, reviewers, submitters).2.3 Establish workflow logic, data models, and database schema to ensure secure handling of proposal data, financial records, stakeholder profiles, and geospatial information.3) Development and Testing3.1 Develop the front-end application, including dashboards, project filtering tools, mapping modules, and data visualization features.3.2 Build the back-end infrastructure with role-based access controls, user authentication, secure data storage, and integrated workflow management.3.3 Conduct internal and external testing, including alpha and beta testing cycles, to validate functionality, identify bugs, and refine system usability based on stakeholder feedback.4) User Acceptance Testing (UAT) and Finalization4.1 Organize stakeholder demos and feedback sessions with GGGI, CCDA, DFAT, and selected CFSC members to validate the system.4.2 Finalize all components based on testing outcomes, ensuring the platform meets agreed performance and quality standards.4.3 Prepare and submit a UAT report summarizing revisions, stakeholder feedback, and user validation outcomes.5) Deployment, Training, and Documentation5.1 Deploy the final, fully functional version of the dashboard on a secure and reliable hosting environment approved by GGGI. The Consultant shall configure the platform to ensure security, performance, scalability, and uptime—along with encrypted data exchange, adequate file storage, and automated backup mechanisms.5.2 Deliver comprehensive user documentation (including manuals, quick-start guides, and SOPs), a system administrator guide, and full technical documentation covering architecture, data schema, user roles, workflows, and maintenance procedures.Note: Training activities and related deliverables are described in detail under the section “Training and Capacity Building.”6) Technical and Hosting RequirementsThe Climate Finance Dashboard must be developed as a secure, scalable, and web-based platform that meets international standards for usability, performance, and cybersecurity. Key technical requirements include: Hosting: The platform shall be hosted on a secure cloud-based environment (e.g., AWS, Azure, or equivalent) or another hosting solution approved by GGGI. The Consultant will recommend the optimal hosting configuration based on performance, cost, and long-term sustainability. Hosting should support high availability, encryption, and sufficient bandwidth and storage capacity to manage concurrent users and large volumes of data and documents. Licensing: The Consultant will be responsible for procuring and managing all necessary software licenses during the development and deployment phase. Use of open-source technologies is encouraged where feasible. The final product must allow for unrestricted future use and ownership transfer to the Government of PNG (via CCDA) or another designated institution, without proprietary limitations. Preference will be given to technologies that are widely adopted and supported by active developer communities or established vendors to ensure long-term maintainability and minimize reliance on proprietary solutions. Database Specification and Capacity Building: The Consultant must specify the type of database to be used (e.g., relational or NoSQL) and include a clear capacity-building plan to ensure CCDA and other designated institutions can manage and maintain the database effectively post-transition. Security: The dashboard must adhere to robust security protocols including user authentication, password management, role-based access control, encrypted communication (e.g., SSL/TLS), secure storage, and compliance with data protection standards. The Consultant must ensure secure system architecture and address any identified vulnerabilities during development and post-deployment support. Storage and Backup: The system should provide scalable storage for proposal documents, project records, and associated data. It must include automated and secure backup solutions to safeguard against data loss and ensure system recovery. Interoperability and Portability: The dashboard should be designed with flexibility to allow future integration with national platforms, donor systems, or MEL databases. It should support the exporting of structured data in widely used formats (e.g., CSV, Excel, PDF) and must be designed for portability if migration to a national server is needed.7) Training and Capacity BuildingThe Consultant will be responsible for delivering structured training sessions tailored to different user groups, including CCDA’s Climate Finance Unit, members of the Climate Finance Steering Committee (CFSC), relevant GGGI staff, and DFAT focal points. Training must cover dashboard functionalities, user roles, workflows, data entry protocols, and report generation. Sessions may be delivered virtually or in person and should include practical exercises using real or test data.The Consultant will also provide supporting materials such as presentation slides, quick reference guides, recorded demonstrations (if feasible), and user manuals. Training should build user confidence and ensure institutional ownership of the system.8) Post-Deployment SupportThe Consultant will provide responsive technical support for a period of twelve (12) months following the launch of the platform. This will include addressing technical bugs, performing minor enhancements, responding to user queries, and maintaining platform performance. A helpdesk mechanism (e.g., email, ticketing system) should be established to manage support requests. The Consultant is expected to submit a final support report at the end of this period, summarizing key issues addressed, usage metrics, and any recommendations for improvement.9) Sustainability and Institutional TransitionTo ensure long-term use and ownership of the dashboard, the Consultant will develop a sustainability roadmap outlining:• Options for long-term hosting and maintenance.• Proposed institutional arrangements for administration and oversight.• Required human and financial resources for continued operations.• Recommendations for future expansion of the system for national use or integration with other government platforms.As part of the handover process, the Consultant shall provide full administrative access credentials, source code (if applicable), system documentation, and any additional tools required to support the transition to a designated host institution (e.g., CCDA). This is intended to ensure continuity, security, and national ownership of the Climate Finance Dashboard.For more details, please refer to the Terms of Reference (TOR) document attached.IMPORTANT TIMELINES:The tender submission deadline is 19 AUGUST, 2025 16:00 HRS KOREAN STANDARD TIME (KST).If any bidder has any request for clarification on the TOR or any part of the tender documents, GGGI will be happy to clarify if they are received on or before 7 days before the deadline (namely: if the tender submission deadline is 16:00 19 Aug, 2025 KST, then the due date for submission of request for clarification is 16:00 12 Aug, 2025 KST).Interested parties will be required to register their details on the GGGI e-Green Procurement Portal (https://in-tendhost.co.uk/gggi).HOW TO OBTAIN THE DOCUMENTS:Documents can be accessed via the e-Green Procurement Portal by selecting ‘View Details’ on the relevant notice and then clicking the ‘Tender Application’ button. The portal will enhance national transparency by making key documents, data, and updates easily available to government agencies, development partners, and the public. It will also play a vital role in supporting coordination and understanding around climate finance, specifically by providing clear guidance on how to access climate finance, including funding sources, application procedures, eligibility criteria, and relevant templates or tools.SCOPE OF WORK:Development of Climate Portal Information Hub The development of the Climate Change Web Portal for Kiribati climate finance will be delivered through a structured set of activities designed to ensure a responsive, secure, and user-friendly digital platform that supports national climate communication, transparency, and stakeholder engagement. The assignment shall encompass key activities below: 1) Inception and Co-Design Phase: The assignment will commence with a series of inception meetings involving MFED, OB, MICT and the GCF Readiness team, and other relevant national stakeholders. These consultations will serve to confirm shared expectations, clarify stakeholder roles, and identify high-level content and functionality priorities. A comprehensive needs assessment will follow, focusing on defining user personas, content types, and technical requirements. This phase will also include a review of existing digital platforms, national climate change policies, and donor reporting frameworks to inform the platform design. The Consultant will submit an inception report detailing the project timeline, proposed site architecture, initial wireframes, CMS configuration strategy, and an overview of user journey pathways. 2) System Architecture and Design: Following inception, the Consultant will design a modular and scalable system using an open-source Content Management System (CMS) such as WordPress or Drupal. The selected CMS must support multilingual content in both English and Kiribati language and allow for non-technical staff to manage content through a user-friendly admin dashboard with customizable roles and permissions. The design process will produce mobile-responsive templates that reflect the national branding and climate themes of Kiribati, using intuitive layouts and custom-designed icons to represent sectors such as energy, agriculture, and water. Visual assets will be sourced with proper licensing or created as custom designs. All components will be aligned to ensure ease of navigation, accessibility, and a clean user experience across devices. 3) Development and Testing: This phase involves full-stack development of the portal based on the agreed design. The Consultant will build all core modules and content pages, including a dynamic homepage with banners, featured projects, a portal introduction, and recent news highlights. A central resources repository will be developed, offering filtered access to national documents, policies, assessments, and toolkits. The portal will also host a blog-style news and events section with a media archive, a partners and stakeholders page showcasing institutional profiles, and a contact and feedback interface featuring a directory and secure contact form. The Consultant will integrate SEO tools, site-wide intelligent search, and document metadata indexing to enhance discoverability. Internal QA testing will precede stakeholder testing cycles to ensure full functionality, accuracy, and usability. 4) User Acceptance Testing (UAT) and Finalization: Once development is complete, the Consultant will coordinate and facilitate user acceptance testing with stakeholders including MFED, OB, MICT and the GCF Readiness team, and key technical staff. During UAT, the Consultant will conduct guided walkthroughs and gather structured feedback on all portal components. Based on this feedback, refinements will be made to the platform’s features, layout, and performance. A comprehensive UAT report will be submitted summarizing the findings, adjustments made, and validation outcomes. 5) Deployment, Training, and Documentation: The finalized portal will be deployed to a secure, cloud-based hosting environment such as AWS or DigitalOcean. Hosting must guarantee 99.9% uptime, automated daily backups, encrypted data transfer (SSL), and scalable performance optimized through a Content Delivery Network (CDN). The Consultant will then conduct targeted training sessions tailored to at least two key user groups. Administrative users will participate in hands-on sessions covering backend content management and system administration, while general users will be introduced to navigation, search tools, and document access. Documentation will include detailed user manuals, quick-start guides, SOPs, and recorded demos if feasible. All source code, configurations, and administrator credentials will be handed over, along with a comprehensive technical documentation package outlining the architecture, user roles, content workflows, and maintenance procedures. 6) Technical and Security Requirements: The portal must meet international standards for cybersecurity, performance, and usability. It will include role-based authentication, secure login protocols, and protection against common vulnerabilities such as cross-site scripting (XSS), SQL injection, and CSRF. The Consultant is responsible for ensuring compliance with data protection standards and for conducting regular vulnerability testing throughout development. Integration with Google Analytics will support data-driven insights, while real-time monitoring tools will track site performance and uptime. The platform must be optimized for mobile devices and low-bandwidth environments, and comply with WCAG 2.1 accessibility standards.7) Post-Deployment Support and Handover: The Consultant will provide a launch support package that includes bug fixing, minor enhancements, and technical helpdesk services via email or ticketing system. At the conclusion of the support period, a final report will be submitted summarizing issues resolved, usage metrics, and recommendations for platform improvement.
